messages:
maya: paging oncall, seeing a sharp spike in 429s from gpu-hotpath in us-west-2 starting ~08:02 UTC. queue length on inference-frontend jumped from ~2k -> 18k in 3m. autoscaler didn't respond. :rotating_light:
infra-oncall: got the page, I'm looking at autoscaler logs and tokenbucket metrics now. can you drop the hotpath pool id?
simon: putting the incident channel on priority, tagging ops-bot for alerts.
ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-042 (GPU saturation, autoscale failed). Severity: P1. Assigned to infra-oncall.
maya: stack: redwood-runtime v4.1 hotpath pool gpu-rt-usw2-hot-01. Customers impacted: a few high-throughput tenants + some PLG traffic. error surface: 429s with body: {\"code\":\"RATE_LIMIT\",\"reason\":\"token_bucket_exhausted\"}
infra-oncall: looking at token_bucket refill rates — they dropped to 0.0 around 08:03 due to rate-config reload failing against config service. autoscaler kept desired=0-> didn't add nodes because it reads capacity tiers from same service.
luis: is this the same rollout from yesterday for tier-mapping? I merged a ratepolicy change at 07:50.
infra-oncall: yes, config version 2026-04-08-07:50 is the one. the config reload returned 500 to all runtime nodes. stacktrace in logs: \n```\nError: config-service unreachable: dial tcp 10.201.9.17:8080: connect: connection refused\nat config_loader.go:142\n```\nmaya: customers seeing request failures for long-running chat and batch inference. CS says one enterprise reported timeouts.
simon: oncall, can we open a temporary bypass so hotpath uses last-known-good policy?
infra-oncall: plan: 1) scale up hotpath pool from reserved standby nodes (manual), 2) toggle rate-tier fallback to legacy policy, 3) increase token_bucket refill and burst for tier=platinum to relieve immediate 429s, 4) move heavy tenants to dedicated fallback route. executing step 1 now.
infra-oncall: running: `./infractl pools scale --pool gpu-rt-usw2-hot-01 --replicas 12 --force`
ops-bot: action acknowledged: pool scale request submitted to orchestration (job id: job-2928).
infra-oncall: scale accepted, nodes provisioning. also bumping token refill: `curl -X POST https://config-svc.internal/v1/overrides -d '{"token_refill":{"platinum":{"rate":4000,"burst":8000}}}'`
luis: warning: that override bypasses safety checks, ok for emergency but watch cost.
maya: doing customer impact call: customer-ops, please prepare blurb for enterprise tenants. Priority: confirm if any data lost (should be no), explain degraded throughput and mitigation steps.
customer-ops: drafting now.
eng-sre: seeing autoscaler controller errors: `panic: nil pointer` in scale_decider.go at 08:04 — looks like the code path didn't handle missing tier metadata when config reload failed. pushing hotfix to controller repo.
infra-oncall: autoscaler restart in progress: `kubectl rollout restart deployment/autoscaler-controller -n infra`
ops-bot: deployment/autoscaler-controller restarted.
infra-oncall: autoscaler is back and picked up the new config fallback. desired replicas moved to 12 -> provisioning completed. queue length decreased to ~3.2k. 429s rate down from 18% -> 4% over 5m.
maya: good. continuing step 4: routing heavy tenants to dedicated pools. oncall, coordinate with sales to notify impacted enterprise.
product: opened an incident page in status.redwood.ai, adding customer-facing note: "We are experiencing degraded inference throughput in us-west-2; mitigation in progress."
eng-sre: pushed a small patch to autoscaler to safely use cached tier metadata if config service fails. PR #482 merged to canary.
infra-oncall: deploying canary of patched autoscaler to us-west-2 hotpath. monitoring logs for NPEs.
luis: revert the ratepolicy rollout from 07:50 and mark the config change as bad. rolling back to config 2026-04-08-07:40.
ops-bot: config rollback executed (config version set to 2026-04-08-07:40).
maya: metrics now trending to normal. 429s at 1.1% and queue ~800. good progress.
customer-ops: sent initial email to impacted enterprise with remediation note and ETA for postmortem.
simon: who will own the postmortem? need L4 RCA: config service hard failure + autoscaler code path lacking fallback + ratepolicy rollout testing gap.
eng-sre: volunteering to drive the postmortem and timeline. will schedule a blameless postmortem and include config-service SLO owners, autoscaler, and release managers.
maya: handoff to eng-sre for follow-up. oncall rotation: infra-oncall, you can close the incident once we confirm steady state for 30m.
infra-oncall: will monitor. marking incident as mitigated in ticket and adding runbook entries: - restore config-service HA, - add canary validation for ratepolicy, - add tokenbucket safety caps.
ops-bot: Incident INC-2026-042 status updated to Mitigated by infra-oncall.
maya: thanks everyone. final note: allocate a dedicated postmortem meeting tomorrow 15:00 UTC. assign eng-sre as owner.
eng-sre: ack, will post summary and action items.
product: marking status page updated to: "Service normal; we are investigating the root cause and will publish a postmortem."
customer-ops: follow-up: enterprise asked for timeline on SLA credits; sales alerted.
infra-oncall: leaving monitoring checks, closing channel for operational chatter. further updates will be in the postmortem doc. :white_check_mark:
